cases.rationale: A physically admissible interior fraction is a positive control.
cases.reference: Project invariant implementation: crates/domains/symthaea-culinary/src/validate.rs

cases.rationale: The defined model uses an inclusive random-close-packing boundary; equality must remain accepted.
cases.reference: Berryman (1983), Physical Review A 27; project parameter in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: A fraction above the configured model limit must be rejected, not silently clamped.
cases.reference: Berryman (1983), Physical Review A 27; project parameter in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: IEEE-754 NaN makes ordinary greater-than comparisons false; the validator must reject it explicitly.
cases.reference: Adversarial numeric regression; project input-integrity invariant

cases.rationale: 70% bread hydration is a valid positive control under the configured model window.
cases.reference: Project parameter in thresholds.rs; culinary thresholds require contextual review

cases.rationale: A plausible ratio formed by two negative masses must not bypass domain checks.
cases.reference: Adversarial numeric regression; project input-integrity invariant

cases.rationale: Hydration has a positive denominator requirement; zero flour cannot be normalized.
cases.reference: Adversarial numeric regression; project input-integrity invariant

cases.rationale: A finite, non-negative ratio can still violate a declared process window.
cases.reference: Project parameter in thresholds.rs; culinary thresholds require contextual review

cases.rationale: The intent and configured pH rule agree for this positive control.
cases.reference: McGee (2004), On Food and Cooking; project parameter in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: A pH value outside the declared numeric domain must not be interpreted as an ordinary dairy state.
cases.reference: Project input-domain invariant in validate.rs

cases.rationale: A finite non-negative nutrient profile below the configured sodium and added-sugar thresholds is a positive control.
cases.reference: Merrill and Watt (1955), USDA Agriculture Handbook 74; FDA 21 CFR 101.9; project thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: A non-finite nutrient quantity must be surfaced as invalid data rather than omitted from threshold checks.
cases.reference: Adversarial numeric regression; project input-integrity invariant

cases.rationale: Finite component inputs whose derived energy overflows must not produce an apparently valid profile.
cases.reference: Atwater factor implementation; numeric overflow regression

cases.rationale: A trajectory exactly at the configured set-point is retained as a positive boundary control.
cases.reference: McGee (2004), On Food and Cooking; project parameter in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: An empty process trajectory is not evidence that a process reached a set-point.
cases.reference: Project input-integrity invariant in validate.rs

cases.rationale: Extremely large finite temperature values must fail the input-envelope guard before set-point logic.
cases.reference: Project input sanity envelope in validate.rs; not a cooking or food-safety threshold

cases.rationale: A time-temperature trajectory below absolute zero is outside the model domain.
cases.reference: Project input-domain invariant in validate.rs

cases.rationale: A valid positive trajectory reaches the configured soft-ball stage window.
cases.reference: McGee (2004), On Food and Cooking; project parameter in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: Out-of-order time values must not be silently skipped by process integration.
cases.reference: Project trajectory integrity invariant in validate.rs

cases.rationale: The configured smoke-point comparison is inclusive at equality; this anchors the implemented behavior without asserting all oils share one value.
cases.reference: Project parameter in thresholds.rs; values vary by refinement and product

cases.rationale: The configured smoke-point constraint must reject a trajectory that exceeds the selected fat's model parameter.
cases.reference: Project parameter in thresholds.rs; not a fire-safety certification

cases.rationale: A non-finite requested target is invalid even when the trajectory is finite.
cases.reference: Project numeric-integrity invariant; Murphy et al. (2004) model parameters

cases.rationale: A finite but absurd-duration trajectory that overflows integrated lethality must be rejected as invalid computation, not treated as successful pathogen reduction.
cases.reference: Murphy et al. (2004) model parameters; project 1000 C input-envelope guard is not a validated process limit

cases.rationale: A valid finite nutrient value above the configured daily-value threshold remains a distinct policy violation.
cases.reference: FDA 21 CFR 101.9; project threshold in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: A valid pH can still conflict with the requested smooth-dairy outcome.
cases.reference: McGee (2004), On Food and Cooking; project parameter in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: A numerically valid trajectory below the requested stage is a modeled process violation, not invalid numeric input.
cases.reference: McGee (2004), On Food and Cooking; project parameter in thresholds.rs

cases.rationale: A constant-temperature model hold at its reference temperature should deliver 3.96 / 0.396 = 10 log reductions, exceeding the configured 7-log model target.
cases.reference: Murphy et al. (2004) D/z model parameters as encoded in thresholds.rs; this is a model positive control, not a cooking protocol

cases.rationale: A finite, internally valid trajectory that delivers less than the requested model target must yield a distinct insufficient-lethality violation.
cases.reference: Murphy et al. (2004) D/z model parameters as encoded in thresholds.rs; model behavior only

cases.rationale: A finite but non-positive user-specified lethality target is invalid and must not bypass target validation.
cases.reference: Project input-integrity invariant in validate.rs
